title: Virtual head movement agrees with tape movement
statement: Let a finite list of segments, a segment index $s$, and a tape position $tp$ be given, with $s$ in range and $tp$ valid for that segment. For either head-movement direction, if the virtual position of $tp$ is less than the virtual-word length plus two, then the virtual position after applying the segment-tape movement equals the position obtained by moving the head by that direction in the bounded virtual input, with movement clamped to its boundary positions.
hypotheses_covered: segs is a finite list of segments
s is a natural number with s < |segs|
tp is a tape position valid for segment s
